title: Lost his sight at 4. Captained India to three World Cups. October 23, 2026.
excerpt: From India's heaviest rocket turning a profit for the first time, to a Mumbai-set story winning a Commonwealth literary prize, to a cancer hospital a US doctor built in his hometown with his own fortune, October 23's five stories are about turning something built for one purpose into something that serves many more.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about repurposing something built for one job into something that does far more - a rocket built for government missions now earning commercial revenue, a chip-packaging deal built on techniques India never attempted before, a hospital built from one family's savings into care for an entire region, a short story set in one city winning recognition across an entire Commonwealth, and a captain who lost his sight as a toddler and spent a career giving other blind cricketers a reason to compete.

October 23, 2022: India's heaviest rocket flew its first paying customer

ISRO's LVM3 carried 36 OneWeb satellites into orbit from Sriharikota - its first fully commercial launch, arranged through NewSpace India Limited - marking India's entry into the global commercial launch services market.

A speculative story set in Mumbai just won one of the world's biggest short-story prizes

Sharon Aruparayil won the Asia regional prize in the 2026 Commonwealth Short Story Prize for 'Mehendi Nights,' published by Granta - putting an Indian setting at the center of one of literature's most internationally diverse competitions.

A US doctor gave his family fortune to build a 300-bed cancer hospital in his hometown

Dr. Sampat Shivangi, a physician based in Jackson, Mississippi, funded a 300-bed cancer hospital in Belagavi, Karnataka, inaugurated by President Droupadi Murmu in January 2025 - serving a rural region where patients once traveled hours for treatment.

A defence company just signed up to build chip-packaging tech India has never made before

Paras Semiconductors signed a Rs 6,200 crore MoU with the Madhya Pradesh government in July 2026 for a facility designed for advanced chip-packaging techniques - 3D heterogeneous integration, hybrid bonding, chiplet integration - that India has barely attempted commercially.

Lost his sight at 4. Captained India to three World Cups

Illuri Ajay Kumar Reddy, blinded in a childhood accident in Andhra Pradesh, captained India's Blind Cricket team to the 2017 T20 World Cup and 2018 Cricket World Cup titles, receiving the Arjuna Award from President Murmu in January 2024.

Five stories, one pattern: a rocket repurposed into a revenue stream, a chip deal reaching for techniques never built in India before, a hospital built from one man's savings into care for a whole region, a single city's story reaching an entire Commonwealth, and a captain who turned his own loss into three World Cup titles for a team most people never think to watch.
